nahhas-irab:63-63.t: فَلَمَّا رَجَعُوا إِلى أَبِيهِمْ قالُوا يا أَبانا مُنِعَ مِنَّا الْكَيْلُ — because he had said to them: فَإِنْ لَمْ تَأْتُونِي بِهِ فَلا كَيْلَ لَكُمْ عِنْدِي. فَأَرْسِلْ مَعَنا أَخانا نَكْتَلْ: an apodosis (jawāb). The original form is نكتال; the ḍamma was removed from the lām because of the jussive (jazm), and the alif was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. This is the reading of the people of the two Sanctuaries (Mecca and Medina), Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim. The Kufans read يكتل with yāʾ. The first is the preference of Abū ʿUbayd, so that all of them are included among those who receive the measure; he claimed that if one says يكتل with yāʾ, it would refer to the brother alone. Abū Jaʿfar said: This does not follow, because the speech must take one of two directions: either the meaning is "So send our brother, that he may receive the measure with us", and so it applies to all of them; or the construction is without anteposition and postposition, in which case there is evidence in the speech for the plural in His words فَإِنْ لَمْ تَأْتُونِي بِهِ فَلا كَيْلَ لَكُمْ عِنْدِي.

nahhas-irab:64-64.t: فَاللَّهُ خَيْرٌ حافِظاً: [accusative] as a specification (bayān). This is the reading of the people of Medina, Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim. The rest of the Kufans read حفظا. The first reading is clearer, just as one says: "He is better than him in lineage (ḥasaban)". حافِظاً is accusative (manṣūb) as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: It may be accusative as a specification (bayān).

nahhas-irab:65-65.t:
ما نَبْغِي: «ما» is in the position of the accusative, and the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: what [more] do we seek by informing you, for the king has treated us kindly, and وهذِهِ بِضاعَتُنا shows that, since رُدَّتْ إِلَيْنا. It is related from ʿAlqama: رُدَّتْ إِلَيْنا with kasra on the rāʾ, because its original form is رددت; when it was assimilated, the vowel of the dāl was shifted onto the rāʾ, just as one says «بيع» in the weak verb. Quṭrub reported, for ضرب زيد, «ضرب» [Translator's note: the variant vocalisation Quṭrub reported is not marked in the unvowelled source].
وَنَزْدادُ كَيْلَ بَعِيرٍ: that is, our brother will go out on a camel and it will be measured out to him upon it. ذلِكَ كَيْلٌ يَسِيرٌ: there are two views on its meaning. One is: easy for the king, i.e. simple. The other is: what we have brought is a small measure that does not suffice us, so we need our brother to go out with us so that it may be increased.

nahhas-irab:66-66.t:
إِلَّا أَنْ يُحاطَ بِكُمْ is in the position of the accusative. Abū Isḥāq said: the meaning is "except for your being surrounded". He said: this makes the requital certain, as when you say: "You only came to me in order to take the dirhams", and "except that you take the dirhams".
قالَ اللَّهُ عَلى ما نَقُولُ وَكِيلٌ: that is, a guardian over the oath.

nahhas-irab:67-67.t: وَقالَ يا بَنِيَّ لا تَدْخُلُوا مِنْ بابٍ واحِدٍ: the soundest thing said about it is that he feared that they would enter all together, and the news of them would reach the supreme king, and some harm would befall them from him, or that whoever saw them gathered together would envy them. There is no sense in [taking it as] the evil eye here, because after it comes وَما أُغْنِي عَنْكُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ; for if what follows the evil eye is authentic, it is from Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

nahhas-irab:68-68.t:
What points you to this is: وَلَمَّا دَخَلُوا مِنْ حَيْثُ أَمَرَهُمْ أَبُوهُمْ ما كانَ يُغْنِي عَنْهُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ.
إِلَّا حاجَةً: an exception not of the same kind as what precedes (munqaṭiʿ). وَإِنَّهُ لَذُو عِلْمٍ لِما عَلَّمْناهُ: that is, regarding the matter of his religion. وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لا يَعْلَمُونَ what Jacob ﷺ knew of the matter of his religion.

nahhas-irab:70-70.t: Al-Akhfash said: the plural of سقاية is سقايا. أَيَّتُهَا الْعِيرُ: that is, the people of the caravan; [what follows] indicates that: إِنَّكُمْ لَسارِقُونَ. The call was not made by Joseph's ﷺ command, because it was a lie.

nahhas-irab:72-72.t:
قالُوا نَفْقِدُ صُواعَ الْمَلِكِ. It is related from Abū Hurayra: قالوا نفقد صاع الملك. Abū al-Ashhab related from Abū Rajāʾ: قالوا نفقد صوع الملك without alif and with a dotted ghayn [Translator's note: the word as printed, صوع, has ʿayn; with dotted ghayn it would be صوغ, as discussed below], and the same is related from Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar. Abū Jaʿfar said: the alif in صواع is redundant (zāʾida), and it means صاع; صاع is more common in people's speech, as [the poet] said:
239-
لا نألم القتل ونجزي به ... الأعداء كيل الصّاع بالصّاع
(We feel no pain at killing, and we repay the enemies for it measure for measure, ṣāʿ for ṣāʿ.)
The plural of صواع is صيعان; the plural of صاع, treated as masculine, is أصواع, and treated as feminine, أصوع. The plural of صوغ is أصواغ, like ثوب / أثواب. صوغ is a maṣdar (verbal noun) meaning موغ [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably مصوغ "something wrought" is intended], just as you say: درهم ضرب, i.e. مضروب (minted). وَلِمَنْ جاءَ بِهِ حِمْلُ بَعِيرٍ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), and likewise وَأَنَا بِهِ زَعِيمٌ. الزّعيم is the guarantor; its origin is from "he claimed (zaʿama) that", i.e. he said it.

nahhas-irab:73-73.t: قالُوا تَاللَّهِ: the tāʾ is a substitute for the wāw, because it is the closest of the augment letters to it. Analogy is not applied to the substitution, so one does not say تالرحمن, because when the Arabs substitute one thing for another, it becomes known [only as heard]; likewise figurative usage is not extended by analogy.

nahhas-irab:74-74.t: قالُوا فَما جَزاؤُهُ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). إِنْ كُنْتُمْ كاذِبِينَ: that is, in your saying "and we are not thieves".

nahhas-irab:75-75.t:
قالُوا جَزاؤُهُ مَنْ وُجِدَ فِي رَحْلِهِ فَهُوَ جَزاؤُهُ: this is a difficult point of grammar, and there are three views on it. One is that «جزاؤه» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, the implied form being: "Its penalty with us is like its penalty with you: that whoever steals is enslaved". It is said that this ruling was in the law of Jacob ﷺ, and that it was so at the beginning of Islam until Allah, Mighty and Majestic, abrogated it with amputation. The second view is that «جزاؤه» is a mubtadaʾ, «من وجد» a second mubtadaʾ, and «فهو جزاؤه» the khabar of the second, the whole clause being the khabar of the first; «من» is conditional, or, if you wish, it means الذي. What refers back to the first mubtadaʾ is the second جزاؤه, the implied form being (فهو) هو; then the pronoun was replaced by the overt noun. Sībawayh recited: [al-Ṭawīl] 240-
لعمرك ما معن بتارك حقّه ... ولا منسئ معن ولا متيسّر
(By your life, Maʿn does not give up his due, nor does Maʿn defer [payment], nor is he lenient.)
Except that in the verse [of the Qur'an] it is better, because had the pronoun been used there the meaning would have become ambiguous, so stating the noun overtly is better for this reason. The third view is that «جزاؤه» is a mubtadaʾ and «من وجد في رحله» stands for [Translator's note: so in the source, «كناية عن رحله», apparently corrupt] its khabar, the implied form being: "Its penalty is the enslavement of the one in whose saddlebag it is found"; so فهو refers to the enslavement, and in the sentence it carries the sense of tawkīd (emphasis), as you say: "The penalty of whoever steals is amputation, that is his penalty", and "this is his penalty".
كَذلِكَ: the kāf is in the position of the accusative, i.e. "We requite the wrongdoers with a requital like that".

nahhas-irab:76-76.t: ثُمَّ اسْتَخْرَجَها: he made it feminine, and there are three views on this. One is that the pronoun refers to the صواع, according to the dialect of those who treat it as feminine; another is that it refers to the سقاية; and the third answer is that it refers to the theft. Al-Ḥasan read ثُمَّ اسْتَخْرَجَها مِنْ وِعاءِ أَخِيهِ with ḍamma on the wāw. Outside the Qur'an «إعاء» is permissible, like «أقّت» and «وقتت»; and «إعاء أخيه» is permissible — this is the dialect of Hudhayl — and similarly «إكاف» and «وكاف». كَذلِكَ كِدْنا لِيُوسُفَ: the kāf is in the position of the accusative, i.e. by his doing this, so that he took his brother, when it would not have been possible for him to take him and detain him with the king without a pretext. He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ما كانَ لِيَأْخُذَ أَخاهُ فِي دِينِ الْمَلِكِ إِلَّا أَنْ يَشاءَ اللَّهُ: (أن) is in the position of the accusative, the implied form being "except by Allah's willing" to show him grace through a stratagem like this. نرفع درجات من نشاء: this is the reading of the people of the two Sanctuaries and the people of Basra. The people of Kufa read نَرْفَعُ دَرَجاتٍ with tanwīn; on their reading it is one of the verbs that take two objects, one of them through a preposition, the implied form being "We raise whom We will to degrees". However, most of the speech of the Arabs follows the first reading: they say "O Allah, raise his degree", and they hardly ever say "O Allah, raise him a degree". Mālik ibn Anas said: I heard Zayd ibn Aslam say about His words, Mighty and Majestic, نَرْفَعُ دَرَجاتٍ مَنْ نَشاءُ: by knowledge. وَفَوْقَ كُلِّ ذِي عِلْمٍ عَلِيمٌ: a mubtadaʾ (subject), and there are two construals: one is "Above everyone possessing knowledge is one more knowledgeable than him", until that ends with Allah, Mighty and Majestic; the other construal is "Above everyone possessing knowledge is One who knows everything", and He is Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

nahhas-irab:77-77.t:
قالُوا إِنْ يَسْرِقْ: jussive (majzūm) by إن, and the apodosis is فَقَدْ سَرَقَ أَخٌ لَهُ مِنْ قَبْلُ. The meaning involves the omission of "saying", the implied form being: "then it has been said, a brother of his stole". Among the best things said about its meaning is that al-Suddī said: Joseph's ﷺ paternal aunt was fond of him, and she had raised him. When he grew up, they wanted to take him from her, so she devised a ruse to prevent them: she took the girdle of Isaac ﷺ and tied it around his waist beneath his clothes. The ruling for a thief who stole was that he be made to serve, so she used this ruse and kept him with her. That is why his brothers said: فَقَدْ سَرَقَ أَخٌ لَهُ مِنْ قَبْلُ. فَأَسَرَّها يُوسُفُ فِي نَفْسِهِ وَلَمْ يُبْدِها لَهُمْ: the scholars have several views on this:
One is that he kept within himself his statement شَرٌّ مَكاناً وَاللَّهُ. It is said: he kept within himself requiting them for what they said about him. It is said: he kept within himself the argument against what they said and did not wish to make his excuse clear in that. And it is said: he kept within himself their statement «فقد سرق أخ له من قبل» and did not wish to broadcast and spread it.
قالَ أَنْتُمْ شَرٌّ مَكاناً: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). مَكاناً is accusative as a specification (bayān), i.e. in deed.

nahhas-irab:78-78.t: إِنَّ لَهُ أَباً شَيْخاً كَبِيراً: [شَيْخاً كَبِيراً is] part of its naʿt (adjective).

nahhas-irab:79-79.t: قالَ مَعاذَ اللَّهِ: a maṣdar (verbal noun). أَنْ نَأْخُذَ is in the position of the accusative, i.e. "from our taking". إِلَّا مَنْ وَجَدْنا: in the position of the accusative by نأخذ. إِنَّا إِذاً لَظالِمُونَ: i.e. if we took someone else.

nahhas-irab:80-80.t:
فَلَمَّا اسْتَيْأَسُوا مِنْهُ خَلَصُوا: that is, they withdrew by themselves, he not being with them. نَجِيًّا: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); it is a singular that stands for a plural, and its plural is أنجية. وَمِنْ قَبْلُ ما فَرَّطْتُمْ فِي يُوسُفَ: «ما» is redundant (zāʾida) with no grammatical position. It is said: it is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), meaning "your failure regarding Joseph occurred" [before]. And it is said its position is accusative, conjoined to «أنّ», the meaning being: "Do you not know that your father took a solemn pledge from you before Allah, and know your failure regarding Joseph, peace be upon him?"
فَلَنْ أَبْرَحَ الْأَرْضَ: that is, from the land. حَتَّى يَأْذَنَ لِي أَبِي: accusative by حتى, which is a substitute for «أن».
أَوْ يَحْكُمَ اللَّهُ لِي: conjoined to «يأذن», and the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: or Allah judges for me that I may pass along with my brother, so that I go with him to my father. وَهُوَ خَيْرُ الْحاكِمِينَ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:81-81.t: ارْجِعُوا إِلى أَبِيكُمْ فَقُولُوا [to] him: يا أَبانا إِنَّ ابْنَكَ سَرَقَ وَما. Abū Ḥātim said: some people mentioned إِنَّ ابْنَكَ سَرَقَ ] [Translator's note: a stray bracket stands here in the source; the variant meant is evidently سُرِّقَ, as the explanation shows], and said its meaning is "he was accused of theft", as one says: "so-and-so was wronged" and "was accused of treachery". He said: but I have not heard a chain of transmission (isnād) for it. Abū Jaʿfar said: his denial of having heard it is no argument against one who has heard it. This word has been transmitted by more than one person, among them Muḥammad ibn Saʿdān the grammarian in his book «Kitāb al-Qirāʾāt», and he is trustworthy and reliable, and he mentioned that it is the reading of Ibn ʿAbbās. Abū Isḥāq said: it was read (إنّ ابنك سرق), and it bears two meanings: one is "theft was known of him", and the other "he was accused of theft". شَهِدْنا إِلَّا بِما عَلِمْنا وَما كُنَّا لِلْغَيْبِ حافِظِينَ: that is, we did not know, at the time we took him from you, that he would steal, [otherwise] we would not have taken him.

nahhas-irab:82-82.t: وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ الَّتِي كُنَّا فِيها: that is, the people of the town. Sībawayh said: but it is not permissible to say "Speak to Hind" when you mean Hind's servant, because this would be ambiguous.

nahhas-irab:83-83.t: قالَ بَلْ سَوَّلَتْ لَكُمْ أَنْفُسُكُمْ أَمْراً: that is, they made it seem fair, without any theft having come from him. فَصَبْرٌ جَمِيلٌ: that is, is more fitting than anguish. عَسَى اللَّهُ أَنْ يَأْتِيَنِي بِهِمْ جَمِيعاً: because he held that Joseph ﷺ had not died, but only that news of him had been hidden from him; for Joseph ﷺ had been carried off as a slave who owned nothing for himself, then the king bought him and he was in his house, not appearing to people, then he was imprisoned. When he became established, he devised a way for his father to learn news of him; he did not send a messenger, because he did not want his brothers to know of that, lest they prevent the messenger from reaching his father. He said «بهم» because they were three: Joseph, his brother, and the one who stayed behind with his brother.

nahhas-irab:84-84.t:
وَتَوَلَّى عَنْهُمْ وَقالَ يا أَسَفى عَلى يُوسُفَ وَابْيَضَّتْ: Abū Isḥāq said: the original form is يا أسفي; the yāʾ was replaced by alif because of the lightness of the alif and the fatḥa. عَيْناهُ مِنَ الْحُزْنِ فَهُوَ. He said: some people asked about the meaning of the intensity of Jacob's ﷺ grief, and the scholars have three answers on this: one is that Jacob ﷺ, when he knew that Joseph, peace be upon him, was alive, regretted that [Translator's note: the text here appears defective; only the first and third answers are given, and the first is incomplete]. The third answer is the clearest of them: that grief is not forbidden; what is forbidden is wailing, tearing the clothes, and speaking what is not fitting. The Prophet ﷺ said:
«The eye sheds tears and the heart grieves, but we do not say what angers the Lord.» And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made it clear by His words:
فَهُوَ كَظِيمٌ.

nahhas-irab:85-85.t:
قالُوا تَاللَّهِ تَفْتَؤُا تَذْكُرُ يُوسُفَ: al-Kisāʾī said: one says فتأت and فتئت أفعل ذلك, i.e. "I have not ceased [doing that]". Al-Farrāʾ claimed that «لا» is implied, and he recited: [al-Ṭawīl] 241-
فقلت يمين الله أبرح قاعدا ... ولو قطعوا رأسي لديك وأوصالي
(So I said: by Allah's oath, I shall not cease sitting, even if they cut off my head and my limbs in your presence.)
What he said is good and sound. Al-Khalīl and Sībawayh held that «لا» is implied in an oath because there is no ambiguity in it: had it been affirmative, it would have had the lām and the nūn. حَتَّى تَكُونَ حَرَضاً: one says حرض and حرض, حروضا and حروضة, when one wastes away and becomes ill; and a man is حارض and حرض — except that حرضا is neither made dual nor plural; similarly قمن and حري are neither made dual nor plural. The lexicographers reported: أحرضه الهمّ, when worry makes him ill; and رجل حارض means a foolish man.

nahhas-irab:86-86.t:
لَ إِنَّما أَشْكُوا بَثِّي [Translator's note: so in the source; the fragment begins with the last letter of قالَ.]
The true sense of البثّ in the language is the destructive things that come upon a person which he is unable to conceal; it is from بثثته, i.e. I scattered it, so a calamity was called بثّ figuratively.

nahhas-irab:87-87.t: يا بَنِيَّ اذْهَبُوا فَتَحَسَّسُوا مِنْ يُوسُفَ وَأَخِيهِ وَلا: that is, go to this one who demanded your brother from you and used a ruse against you in taking him, and ask him about him and about his course.

nahhas-irab:88-90.t: فَلَمَّا دَخَلُوا عَلَيْهِ قالُوا يا أَيُّهَا الْعَزِيزُ: that is, the one who is inaccessible (powerful). مَسَّنا وَأَهْلَنَا الضُّرُّ: so they humbled themselves before him and were lowly, and he was moved, so قالَ هَلْ عَلِمْتُمْ ما فَعَلْتُمْ بِيُوسُفَ وَأَخِيهِ إِذْ أَنْتُمْ جاهِلُونَ. It is said: this indicated that they were young at the time they took Joseph, peace be upon him, such that they left his brother alone apart from him, unable to stand against them. Then they became aware, and قالُوا أَإِنَّكَ لَأَنْتَ يُوسُفُ, with lightening of the second hamza; it is also permissible to pronounce both fully, and to insert an alif between them; and «إنك» as a statement is permissible. إِنَّهُ مَنْ يَتَّقِ وَيَصْبِرْ: the hāʾ is a pronoun referring to the matter (al-ḥadīth), and the clause is the khabar (predicate); likewise the clause is the khabar in His words, Mighty and Majestic: فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُضِيعُ أَجْرَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ.

nahhas-irab:91-91.t: قالُوا تَاللَّهِ لَقَدْ آثَرَكَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْنا: the original has two hamzas; the second was lightened, and it is not permissible to pronounce both fully. The active participle is مؤثر and the maṣdar (verbal noun) is إيثار. One says أثرت التراب إثارة, so I am مثير; this too is on the pattern أفعل, then made weak: the original is أثير; the vowel of the yāʾ was shifted to the thāʾ, the yāʾ became alif, then it was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. And أثرت الحديث is on the pattern فعلت, so I am آثره. وَإِنْ كُنَّا لَخاطِئِينَ: from خطئ يخطأ, when one commits a sin (khaṭīʾa).

nahhas-irab:92-92.t: قالَ لا تَثْرِيبَ عَلَيْكُمُ الْيَوْمَ: the sentence ends here, and the meaning of اليوم is "the time". يَغْفِرُ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ: an imperfect verb carrying the sense of supplication.

nahhas-irab:93-93.t:
اذْهَبُوا بِقَمِيصِي هذا: هذا is a naʿt (adjective) of القميص, and قميص is masculine. As for the poet's words:
[al-Kāmil] 242-
يدعو هوازن والقميص مفاضة ... فوق النّطاق تشدّ بالأزرار
(He calls on Hawāzin, while the shirt is an ample [coat of mail] over the belt, fastened with buttons.)
its implied form is "and the shirt is an ample coat of mail". يَأْتِ بَصِيراً: the apodosis of the imperative. وَأْتُونِي بِأَهْلِكُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ: tawkīd (emphasis) in the position of the genitive; it may not be accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), because it follows what precedes it.

nahhas-irab:96-96.t: فَلَمَّا أَنْ جاءَ الْبَشِيرُ: «أن» is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis. فَارْتَدَّ بَصِيراً: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:99-100.t: آوى إِلَيْهِ أَبَوَيْهِ: accusative by the verb, and likewise وَرَفَعَ أَبَوَيْهِ. سُجَّداً: as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:101-101.t:
رَبِّ قَدْ آتَيْتَنِي مِنَ الْمُلْكِ: [رَبِّ] is in the position of the accusative because it is a vocative in a genitive construct (iḍāfa), the implied form being يا ربّ.
فاطِرَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ: accusative as a naʿt (adjective); or, if you wish, it is a second vocative.

nahhas-irab:102-102.t: ذلِكَ: mubtadaʾ (subject). مِنْ أَنْباءِ الْغَيْبِ: its khabar (predicate). نُوحِيهِ إِلَيْكَ: a second khabar. Abū Isḥāq said: «ذلك» may also mean الذي, with نُوحِيهِ إِلَيْكَ as its khabar, i.e. "that which is of the tidings of the unseen, We reveal it to you".

nahhas-irab:103-103.t: وَما أَكْثَرُ النَّاسِ: the noun of «ما». وَلَوْ حَرَصْتَ: that is, for their guidance. بِمُؤْمِنِينَ: the khabar (predicate) of ما.

nahhas-irab:105-106.t: وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ آيَةٍ فِي السَّماواتِ: al-Khalīl and Sībawayh said it is «أي» with the kāf of comparison entering upon it, so that it came to mean «كم». Abū Jaʿfar said: one may not pause on it except [as] وكأيّ, just as you say أنت كزيد, and none of the Arabs says أنت كزيدن with a nūn. The grammarians have given a reason for this, saying: one does not pause on the tanwīn lest it resemble the nūn that bears the case ending; however, rawm (a faint vowel) and ishmām (lip-rounding) are permissible in the nominative, and rawm in the genitive, while making it quiescent in the genitive is better. Most of what occurs in the speech and poetry of the Arabs is «كائن» من رجل قد رأيته, on the pattern of كاع. A group of the imams of the Muslims read according to this dialect, among them Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, Ibn Kathīr, Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba, al-Aʿraj and al-Aʿmash. It is related from Ibn Muḥayṣin: وكئن on the pattern of كعن. This was done to this word because of its frequency in their speech. It is also related from al-Ḥasan: وكاين without hamza. وَهُمْ عَنْها مُعْرِضُونَ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), i.e. they do not reflect; and He made clear that they do not reflect by His words, Mighty and Majestic: وَما يُؤْمِنُ أَكْثَرُهُمْ بِاللَّهِ إِلَّا وَهُمْ مُشْرِكُونَ (106): when it is said to them, "Who created you and created the heavens and the earth?", they say, "Allah, Mighty and Majestic", and then they associate others with Him.

nahhas-irab:107-107.t:
أَوْ تَأْتِيَهُمُ السَّاعَةُ بَغْتَةً: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and its origin is a maṣdar (verbal noun). Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said:
A ḥāl after an indefinite noun has come from the Arabs, namely their saying: وقع أمر بغتة وفجأة (a matter happened suddenly, unexpectedly). Abū Jaʿfar said:
The meaning of بغتة is: it struck him from where he did not expect.

nahhas-irab:108-108.t: قُلْ هذِهِ سَبِيلِي: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). أَنَا: tawkīd (emphasis). وَمَنِ اتَّبَعَنِي: conjoined to the latent pronoun.

nahhas-irab:109-109.t: وَلَدارُ الْآخِرَةِ: mubtadaʾ (subject); خَيْرٌ is its khabar (predicate). Al-Farrāʾ claimed that الدار is the same as الآخرة, i.e. a thing is annexed to itself. Al-Kisāʾī cited as evidence their saying صلاة الأولى, and al-Akhfash cited their saying مسجد الجامع. Abū Jaʿfar said: annexing a thing to itself is impossible, because a thing is annexed only to something else so as to be made known by it. The better form is الصلاة الأولى, because it was the first prayer performed when the prayers were made obligatory, and the first that was made manifest; for that reason it is also called ظهر. The implied form is: "and the abode of the state of the Hereafter is better".

nahhas-irab:110-110.t: حَتَّى إِذَا اسْتَيْأَسَ الرُّسُلُ وَظَنُّوا أَنَّهُمْ قَدْ كُذِبُوا: this is the clear reading, conjoined to استيأس, and among the Companions ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, read it. Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah have mercy on them, read وَظَنُّوا أَنَّهُمْ قَدْ كُذِبُوا, the implied form being "and their peoples thought that the messengers had been lied to". Mujāhid read وَظَنُّوا أَنَّهُمْ قَدْ كُذِبُوا, i.e. "and their peoples thought that the messengers had lied", when they saw Allah's, Mighty and Majestic, bounty in delaying the punishment. [Translator's note: the source prints all three readings with the same vowelling; the intended variants are presumably كُذِّبُوا, كُذِبُوا and كَذَبُوا respectively.] It is related from ʿĀṣim: فَنُجِّيَ مَنْ نَشاءُ with a single nūn, and (من) is in the position of the nominative as the noun whose agent is not named (nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent).

nahhas-irab:111-111.t: وَلكِنْ تَصْدِيقَ الَّذِي بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ: that is, "but it was"; the nominative is also permissible, meaning "but it is a confirmation of what was before it". وَتَفْصِيلَ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَهُدىً وَرَحْمَةً لِقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t: The implied form (taqdīr) is: هذا ("this [is]"); (تِلْكَ آياتُ الْكِتابِ) is on the pattern of mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:10-10.t:
The people of Mecca, the people of Basra and the people of Kufa read (فِي غَيابَتِ الْجُبِّ), and the people of Medina read في غيابات الجبّ. Abū ʿUbayd allowed [only] the singular, because it refers to a single spot into which they cast him, and he rejected the plural for this reason. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is a narrowing of the language. غيابات is plural, and it is permissible on two grounds. Sībawayh related: سير عليه عشيّانات وأصيلانات ("he was made to travel through evenings and late afternoons"), meaning عشيّة and أصيل, making every moment of it an evening and a late afternoon; so likewise every spot that hides is made a غيابة and then put in the plural. The other ground is that in the pit there are many hidden recesses. One says: غاب يغيب غيبا وغيابة وغيابا, as [the poet] said:
[al-Ṭawīl] 228-
ألا فالبثا شهرين أو نصف ثالث ... إلى ذا كما ما غيّبتني غيابيا
(Stay, you two, two months or half a third, beside this — as long as my hiding-place does not hide me)
(يَلْتَقِطْهُ) is the response to the imperative. Mujāhid, Abū Rajāʾ, al-Ḥasan and Qatāda read تلتقطه بعض السيارة (with the feminine prefix), and this is construed according to the sense, because "some of the caravan" is a caravan [i.e. feminine]. Sībawayh related: سقطت بعض أصابعه ("some of his fingers fell [fem.]"), and he recited: [al-Ṭawīl] 229-
وتشرق بالقول الّذي قد أذعته ... كما شرقت صدر القناة من الدّم
(And you choke on the word you have spread abroad, as the shaft's upper part chokes [fem.] on blood)
(إِنْ كُنْتُمْ) is in the position of the jussive by the condition. (فاعِلِينَ) is the khabar (predicate) of (كنتم).

nahhas-irab:2-2.t:
(إِنَّا أَنْزَلْناهُ قُرْآناً عَرَبِيًّا): (قرآن) is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), that is, "collected together"; and it may be a preparatory element (tawṭiʾa) for the ḥāl, as you say: مررت بزيد رجلا صالحا ("I passed by Zayd, a righteous man"). (عَرَبِيًّا) is a ḥāl. The meaning of أعرب is "he made clear", and from it is «الثّيّب تعرب عن نفسها» ("the previously-married woman makes clear [her wish] for herself"). (لَعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ): so that you may be in hope of this. Some of the Arabs bring أن with لعلّ, likening it to عسى; and the lām in لعلّ is redundant (zāʾida), for emphasis, as [the poet] said:
[al-Rajaz] 225-
يا أبتا علّك أو عساكا
(O my father, perhaps you, or it may be that you…)

nahhas-irab:3-3.t:
(نَحْنُ) is a mubtadaʾ (subject). (نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ) is in the position of the khabar (predicate). (أَحْسَنَ الْقَصَصِ) is in the sense of the maṣdar (verbal noun), the implied form being: قصصا أحسن القصص ("a relating, the best of relating").
(بِما أَوْحَيْنا إِلَيْكَ): al-Akhfash said: that is, "by Our revealing to you". (هذَا الْقُرْآنَ) is accusative by (أوحينا). Al-Farrāʾ permitted the genitive, saying: as a repetition (takrīr), and with the Basrans that is as a badal (substitute) from «ما»; and Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] permitted the nominative, with an implied (muḍmar) mubtadaʾ. (وَإِنْ كُنْتَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ لَمِنَ الْغافِلِينَ), that is, among those unaware of what We have made known to you.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t:
(إِذْ) is in the position of the accusative as an adverb (ẓarf). (قالَ يُوسُفُ): it is a diptote (not inflected for nunation) because it is non-Arabic. Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif read إذ قال يؤسف with hamza and a kasra on the sīn, and Abū Zayd related «يؤسف» with hamza and a fatḥa on the sīn. (لِأَبِيهِ) is genitive by the lām, and the sign of its genitive is the yāʾ; what is omitted from it is a wāw, as shown by أبوان ("two fathers/parents"). (يا أَبَتِ) with a kasra on the tāʾ is the reading of ʿĀṣim, Nāfiʿ, Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī and al-Aʿmash; Abū Jaʿfar, al-Aʿraj and ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir read (يا أَبَتَ) with a fatḥa on the tāʾ; and al-Farrāʾ permitted «يا أبتُ» with a ḍamma on the tāʾ. Abū Jaʿfar said: when you say يا أبتِ with a kasra on the tāʾ, the tāʾ according to Sībawayh stands in place of the yāʾ of annexation (the first-person possessive), and on his view pausing is only permissible with the hāʾ. He has proofs for his view, among them: that your saying «يا أبت» conveys the meaning of your saying يا أبي ("O my father"); that one does not say يا أبة except in the definite; that one does not say جاءني أبة ("an abat came to me") — the Arabs use this only in the vocative specifically; and that one does not say يا أبتي, because the tāʾ is a substitute for the yāʾ, so the two are not combined. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that when one says يا أبتِ with kasra, he pauses on the tāʾ and nothing else, because the yāʾ is intended. Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] claimed this is an error, and what he said is right: how could it be intended when one does not say يا أبتا? As for our saying "with a kasra on the tāʾ" and not "a kasra on the hāʾ", that is because the kasra occurs only in continuous speech (idrāj); if you said مررت بامرأة ("I passed by a woman") you would say: the sign of the genitive is the kasra of the tāʾ, and none would say "the kasra of the hāʾ" except one who does not know.
يا أبتَ with a fatḥa on the tāʾ is problematic in grammar, and there are several views on it:
The doctrine of Sībawayh is that they likened this hāʾ, which is a substitute for the yāʾ, to the hāʾ that is the sign of the feminine, and so they said يا أبتَ, just as [the poet] said: [al-Ṭawīl] 226-
كليني لهمّ يا أميمة ناصب
(Leave me, O Umayma, to a wearying care)
This is one of the two views of al-Farrāʾ. He has another view, which is the view of Quṭrub, Abū ʿUbayda and Abū Ḥātim: that the original is يا أبتاه and then the alif was dropped. On [this] view the pause according to al-Farrāʾ is on the tāʾ and nothing else, and on the view in which he agreed with Sībawayh it is on the hāʾ, according to both of them, and nothing else. This view [i.e. that the original is يا أبتاه] is an error, because this is not a context of lamentation (nudba), and the alif is light and is not dropped. Quṭrub also said about يا أبتَ with fatḥa: the original is يا أبتاً, and then the tanwīn (nunation) was dropped. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is what is not permissible, because tanwīn is not dropped without a cause, and moreover tanwīn enters only on the indefinite, and one does not say in the indefinite يا أبة. On the fatḥa there is a fourth view, which seems the best of them: that the original is the kasra, and then a fatḥa was substituted for the kasra, just as an alif is substituted for the yāʾ, so that for يا غلامي أقبل ("O my boy, come forward") one says: يا غلاما أقبل. Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] claimed that يا أبةُ with ḍamma is not permissible. Abū Jaʿfar said: in my view that is not ruled out; just as Sībawayh permitted the fatḥa by likening it to the hāʾ of the feminine, so the ḍamma is also permissible by likening it to it.
(إِنِّي رَأَيْتُ أَحَدَ عَشَرَ كَوْكَباً): there is no disagreement among the grammarians [about its being invariable], since one says: جاءني أحد عشر and مررت بأحد عشر, and likewise ثلاثة عشر to تسعة عشر and what lies between them. Al-Farrāʾ held that when they joined one of the two nouns to the other, they disliked inflecting the first, lest it leave the category of numbers, and they disliked inflecting the second, lest it resemble بعلبكّ; so they gave them both a single vowel, as they had been before the joining into an invariable (mabnī) form. Al-Kisāʾī said: the accusative is the sink of grammar — whenever something is turned from its proper course, it is put in the accusative. The Basrans said: the fatḥa is the lightest of the vowels, so when one of the two nouns was joined to the other they were given the lightest of the vowels. Some of them said: when the wāw [i.e. the conjunction "and"] was dropped, and it was vowelled with fatḥa, they gave the two nouns its vowel. There is no disagreement among the Basrans that this is made definite by placing the alif and lām at its beginning, so you say:
مضى الأحد عشر رجلا ("the eleven men passed") and nothing else, while al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ permitted مضى الأحد العشر. Al-Farrāʾ said: because they imagine the one as separate from the other. He also permitted placing the alif and lām on the tamyīz (specification).
That is impossible according to the Basrans, because the tamyīz is a singular that indicates a plural, and if it were definite it would not carry this meaning. Al-Farrāʾ said: if you annex it to yourself [i.e. to the first-person pronoun], you inflect the first, and say: هذه خمسةُ عشري ("these are my fifteen") and مررت بخمسةِ عشري. He said: since it is not permissible to annex it to the first [element], because عشر lies between them, you inflect the first; and the tamyīz is not permissible here because their inflections differ. Abū Jaʿfar said: this invalidates everything that has gone before. I heard Muḥammad ibn al-Walīd say: I heard Abū al-ʿAbbās [al-Mubarrad] say: Ismāʿīl ibn Isḥāq would sometimes read to me something of al-Farrāʾ's words and I would find it good, but he would not reach the end of it before spoiling it.
Sībawayh said: Know that the Arabs keep خمسة عشر and what resembles it in one state with the alif and lām and with annexation. The reason, according to his followers, is that the respect for which it was made invariable is still present with the alif and lām and with annexation. Sībawayh related: هذه خمسة عشرُك with the second [element] in the nominative. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that one says: ما رأيت خمسةَ عشرٍ قطّ خيرا منها ("I have never seen a fifteen better than it") with عشر in the genitive and with tanwīn. He said: and the tamyīz does not enter here. Abū Jaʿfar said: this too is not permissible according to the Basrans.
Abū Jaʿfar [the reader] and al-Ḥasan read (إِنِّي رَأَيْتُ أَحَدَ عْشَرَ) with a sukūn on the ʿayn. Al-Akhfash and al-Farrāʾ claimed that they found the vowels heavy and dropped [one] when they became many. Abū Jaʿfar said: Sībawayh did not mention this; rather, by the text of his words it must not be permissible, because he said: أحد عشر is like أحد جمل ("one camel"), and in his view dropping the fatḥa is not permissible because of its lightness.
(وَالشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ) is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it. (رَأَيْتُهُمْ) is a tawkīd (emphasis). And He said (رَأَيْتُهُمْ لِي ساجِدِينَ), coming in the masculine [rational plural]. The view of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh is that since obedience and prostration — both acts of rational beings — were predicated of these things, they were given what applies to rational beings.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: (يا بُنَيَّ لا تَقْصُصْ) is a prohibition. The doubling appears [unassimilated] because the second [ṣād] has become quiescent; outside the Qurʾān assimilation is permissible, with fatḥa, kasra and ḍamma. (رُؤْياكَ) is with hamza, and the plural is رؤى. Abū Ḥātim said: Yaʿqūb said: Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, may Allah have mercy on him, said: the people of the Ḥijāz do not pronounce the hamza in «رؤيا», while Bakr and Tamīm pronounce it. Abū Ḥātim said: one also says ريّا, turning the wāw into a yāʾ with the rāʾ in ḍamma, and one says ريّا with a kasra on the rāʾ. (فَيَكِيدُوا) is the response to the prohibition with the fāʾ, and we have mentioned it. (كَيْداً) is a maṣdar (verbal noun). (إِنَّ الشَّيْطانَ لِلْإِنْسانِ عَدُوٌّ مُبِينٌ): the noun of «إنّ» and its khabar (predicate). The plural of عدوّ is أعداء; its proper course would have been to form its plural on the pattern فُعول, but that was found heavy in it. «[Translator's note: the source prints «جواب النبي» ("the response to the Prophet"), evidently a misprint for «جواب النهي» ("the response to the prohibition"), and «ريا» without marking which form is meant; translated per the context.]»

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: (وَكَذلِكَ يَجْتَبِيكَ رَبُّكَ): the kāf is in the position of the accusative, because it is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun); likewise the kāf in (كَما أَتَمَّها), and (ما) is restrictive (kāffa).

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: The people of Medina, the people of Basra and the people of Kufa read (لَقَدْ كانَ فِي يُوسُفَ وَإِخْوَتِهِ آياتٌ لِلسَّائِلِينَ), and the people of Mecca read آية للسائلين in the singular. Abū ʿUbayd chose «آيات», saying: because they are many lessons. Abū Jaʿfar said: «آية» here is a good reading, that is: there was indeed, in those who asked about the story of Yūsuf, a sign in what they were told; for they asked the Prophet ﷺ while he was in Mecca, saying: "Tell us about a man among the prophets who was in Syria, whose son was taken out to Egypt, and he wept over him until he became blind." There was no one in Mecca from the People of the Book nor anyone who knew the stories of the prophets; rather, the Jews had sent [people] to him from Medina to ask him about this. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed Sūrat Yūsuf all at once, containing everything in the Torah about his story and more, and that was a sign for the Prophet ﷺ comparable to ʿĪsā's ﷺ bringing the dead to life. «[Translator's note: the source prints «واختار أبي عبيد», with أبي for أبو.]»

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: (إِذْ قالُوا لَيُوسُفُ) is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and this is the lām of emphasis. (وَأَخُوهُ) is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it. (أَحَبُّ إِلى أَبِينا) is its khabar (predicate); it is not put in the dual or the plural, because it has the sense of the verb.

nahhas-irab:9-9.t:
(أَوِ اطْرَحُوهُ أَرْضاً): «أرضا» is accusative by the omission of «في», not as an adverb (ẓarf), because it is not indeterminate (mubham). Sībawayh recited, among the examples in which في is omitted: [al-Kāmil] 227-
لدن بهزّ الكفّ يعسل متنه ... فيه كما عسل الطّريق الثّعلب
(Supple, its shaft quivers at the shake of the hand, as the fox runs quivering along the road)
Except that in the verse [of the Qurʾān] it is good and frequent, because the verb takes two objects, one of them through a particle, and when you omit the particle the verb passes over directly to the other. (يَخْلُ لَكُمْ) is jussive (majzūm) because it is the response to the imperative; that is why the wāw has been dropped from it. (وَتَكُونُوا) is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ and ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd read (قالُوا يا أَبانا ما لَكَ لا تَأْمَنَّا) with assimilation (idghām) and without ishmām (rounding the lips to indicate the ḍamma). Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif read ما لك لا تأمننا with two overt nūns. Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb and Abū Razīn read — and it is also related from al-Aʿmash — ما لك لا تيمنّا with a kasra on the tāʾ. All the other people, as far as I know, read with assimilation and ishmām. Abū Jaʿfar said: the first reading, with assimilation and without ishmām, is the analogical one (qiyās), because what is assimilated must be quiescent. Abū ʿUbayda said: there must be ishmām. This view is rejected by the grammarians. Abū Ḥātim said: had it been a true assimilation, it would not have had any ishmām; this too is an error according to the grammarians, because the ishmām comes only after the assimilation, and serves only to indicate that the verb was in the nominative (indicative). تأمننا is according to the original form; «وتيمنّا» is the dialect of Tamīm, who say: أنت تضرب ("you strike"), and we have mentioned it before. «[Translator's note: the source prints «أنت تضرب» unvocalized; the point is the Tamīmī kasra on the imperfect prefix.]»

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: (أَرْسِلْهُ مَعَنا غَداً): it is accusative as an adverb (ẓarf). Its original form according to Sībawayh is «غدو», and this has been used in speech. Al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl said: what lies between dawn and the morning prayer is called غدوة, and likewise بكرة. نرتعْ ونلعبْ, with nūn and a sukūn on the ʿayn, is the reading of the people of Basra; the well-known reading of the people of Mecca is نرتعِ with nūn and a kasra on the ʿayn; the reading of the people of Kufa is (يَرْتَعْ وَيَلْعَبْ) with yāʾ and a sukūn on the ʿayn; and the reading of the people of Medina is يرتعِ ويلعبْ with yāʾ and a kasra on the ʿayn. Abū Jaʿfar said: the first reading is from the Arabs' saying: رتع الإنسان والبعير ("the man and the camel grazed freely") when they eat as they please; except that Maʿmar related from Qatāda, who said: يرتع means "he runs". Abū Jaʿfar said: he took this from His saying «إنا ذهبنا نستبق» ("we went racing"), because the meaning is: we race in running to a particular goal. Likewise «يرتع» with a sukūn on the ʿayn, except that it refers to Yūsuf ﷺ alone. And نرتعِ with a kasra on the ʿayn is from الرِّعي, which is pasture, while الرَّعي is the maṣdar (verbal noun). Al-Qutabī [Ibn Qutayba] said: نرتعِ means "we guard and watch over one another", from their saying رعاك الله, that is, "may Allah guard you". Abū Jaʿfar said: the sign of the jussive in نرتع and يرتع is the ḍamma, and it is jussive (majzūm) because it is the response to (أرسله); and the sign of the jussive in نرتعِ and يرتعِ is the dropping of the yāʾ. (وَيَلْعَبْ) is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it. (وَإِنَّا لَهُ) is a clarification (tabyīn). (لَحافِظُونَ) is the khabar (predicate) of «إنّ». «[Translator's note: «الضمّة» (the ḍamma) as the sign of the jussive is as printed in the source; for the sukūn readings one would expect "the sukūn". The second statement refers to the kasra readings (نرتعِ / يرتعِ, from رعى), whose final yāʾ is dropped.]»

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: (قالَ إِنِّي لَيَحْزُنُنِي) is the most eloquent usage; Yaʿqūb and others related it. (أَنْ تَذْهَبُوا بِهِ) is in the position of the nominative, that is, "your going away with him". (وَأَخافُ أَنْ يَأْكُلَهُ الذِّئْبُ): from تذاءبت الريح, "the wind came from every direction" — so said Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā [Thaʿlab]. He said: «الذئب» has a hamza because it comes from every direction. Warsh related from Nāfiʿ «الذيب» without hamza: since the hamza is quiescent and preceded by a kasra, he lightened it, and it became a yāʾ.

nahhas-irab:16-17.t: (عِشاءً) is an adverb (ẓarf). (يَبْكُونَ) is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said: (وَلَوْ كُنَّا) means "even if we were" (وإن كنّا).

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: (وَجاؤُ عَلى قَمِيصِهِ بِدَمٍ كَذِبٍ) is figurative (majāz), that is, "with blood of falsehood", like (وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ) [Yūsuf: 82]. (فَصَبْرٌ جَمِيلٌ): Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: that is, "my affair", or "what I hold to", is beautiful patience. Quṭrub said: that is, "my patience is beautiful patience". Abū Ḥātim said: ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read, as Sahl ibn Yūsuf claimed, فصبرا جميلا (accusative). He said: and likewise al-Ashhab al-ʿUqaylī; and he said: likewise in the codex of Anas and of Abū Ṣāliḥ. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said: «فصبر جميل» in the nominative is preferable to the accusative, because the meaning is: "what I have is beautiful patience". He said: the accusative is the preferred choice only in a command, as He, Majestic and Mighty, said: (فَاصْبِرْ صَبْراً جَمِيلًا) [al-Maʿārij: 5]. Abū Jaʿfar said: the accusative is as a maṣdar (verbal noun) [i.e. mafʿūl muṭlaq]. (وَاللَّهُ الْمُسْتَعانُ) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). (عَلى ما تَصِفُونَ) is figurative, and the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: Allah is the One whose help is sought in bearing what you describe.

nahhas-irab:19-19.t:
(وَجاءَتْ سَيَّارَةٌ): it is made feminine according to the wording; (فَأَرْسَلُوا وارِدَهُمْ): it is made masculine according to the sense; had it been فأرسلت واردها, it would have been according to the wording. (فَأَدْلى دَلْوَهُ): [the root] is among those with wāw, except that it reverted to yāʾ when it exceeded three letters, following the imperfect; this is the view of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh. The Kufans said: when it became heavy it was turned back to yāʾ, because it is lighter than wāw. The plural of دلو for a small number is أدلٍ; when they are many you say:
دُليّ and دِليّ, the wāw being turned into yāʾ because change is the norm in the plural, and to distinguish between singular and plural; and دلاء, where the wāw was turned into alif and then replaced by a hamza so that two quiescent letters would not meet. (قالَ يا بُشْرايَ هذا غُلامٌ): this is the reading of the people of Medina and the people of Basra, except that Ibn Abī Isḥāq read يا بشريَّ هذا غلام, turning the alif into yāʾ, because this yāʾ [of the first person] puts a kasra on what precedes it; since a kasra on the alif is not possible, turning it [into yāʾ] was a compensation. The people of Kufa read (يا بُشْرى هذا غُلامٌ). There are two views on its meaning: one is that it is the name of a boy [i.e. a companion called Bushrā], and the other is that the meaning is "O good tidings!" Qatāda said: when the bucket was let down, Yūsuf ﷺ clung to it, and when he brought him out he gave them the good tidings, saying: يا بشرى هذا غلام. Abū Jaʿfar said: this view is preferable, because the Qurʾān names anyone only rarely; rather, it comes with allusion (kināya), as He, Majestic and Mighty, said: (وَيَوْمَ يَعَضُّ الظَّالِمُ عَلى يَدَيْهِ) [al-Furqān: 27], who is ʿUqba ibn Abī Muʿayṭ, and after it (يا وَيْلَتى لَيْتَنِي لَمْ أَتَّخِذْ فُلاناً خَلِيلًا) [al-Furqān: 28 «[Translator's note: the source gives 27 for both]»], who is Umayya ibn Khalaf; so it comes by allusion. (وَأَسَرُّوهُ): the hāʾ refers to Yūsuf; as for the wāw, it refers to his brothers, and it has been said: to the merchants who bought him. (بِضاعَةً) is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: the meaning is "they bought him, making him merchandise"; others said: بضاعة means "taken as merchandise".

nahhas-irab:20-20.t:
(وَشَرَوْهُ بِثَمَنٍ بَخْسٍ): [بخس] is a naʿt (adjective) of (ثمن), that is, "of deficiency", that is, small. (دَراهِمَ) is a badal (substitute). One also says دراهيم, as the plural of دراهم; according to Sībawayh it may also be a noun of collective sense, and also according to him it may be that the kasra was lengthened and became a yāʾ. This is not like lengthening the short-alif noun (maqṣūr), because lengthening the maqṣūr is not permissible according to the Basrans, neither in poetry nor elsewhere. The grammarians recited: [al-Basīṭ] 230-
تنفي يداها الحصى في كلّ هاجرة ... نفي الدّراهيم تنقاد الصّياريف
(Her forelegs scatter the pebbles in every midday heat, as the money-changers' testing scatters the dirhams)
(مَعْدُودَةٍ) is a naʿt. (وَكانُوا فِيهِ مِنَ الزَّاهِدِينَ): Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: «فيه» is not included in the ṣila (relative clause) [of the al- in الزاهدين] but is a clarification (tabyīn), that is, "their lack of desire for him". Sībawayh and al-Kisāʾī related زهِدت فيه and زهَدت, with kasra and fatḥa on the hāʾ. «[Translator's note: the source prints «دراهيم على أنه جمع دراهم»; the sense requires «درهام» as the singular of دراهيم. "Kasra and fatḥa on the hāʾ" is as printed; the vowel in question is on the hāʾ of زهد.]»

nahhas-irab:21-21.t:
(وَكَذلِكَ): the kāf is in the position of the accusative. (مَكَّنَّا لِيُوسُفَ), that is, by inclining towards him the heart of the king who bought him, so that he was empowered to command and forbid in the land over which the king ruled. (وَلِنُعَلِّمَهُ مِنْ تَأْوِيلِ الْأَحادِيثِ) is accusative by the lām of purpose (lām kay), and it must be attached (mutaʿalliq) to a verb, so the implied form is: "and so that We might teach him the interpretation of events, We established him". The meaning is: We established him in order to reveal Our speech to him and teach him its interpretation and explanation, and the interpretation of dreams.
And the statement is complete. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: (وَاللَّهُ غالِبٌ عَلى أَمْرِهِ), that is, He does what He wills in His creation; no one is able to prevent Him or overcome Him, and this does not belong to created beings. This is the meaning of "predominant over His affair".

nahhas-irab:22-22.t:
(وَلَمَّا بَلَغَ أَشُدَّهُ): according to Sībawayh it is a plural whose singular is شدّة. Al-Kisāʾī said: its singular is شدّ, as [the poet] said: [al-Kāmil] 230 m-
عهدي به شدّ النّهار كأنّما ... خضب البنان ورأسه بالعظلم
(My last sight of him was at the height of day, as though his fingertips and head were dyed with indigo)
Abū ʿUbayda claimed that it has no singular from its own wording among the Arabs. Its meaning is the completion of strength, after which comes decline. Mujāhid and Qatāda said: al-ashudd is thirty-three years; Rabīʿa, Zayd ibn Aslam and Mālik ibn Anas said: al-ashudd is reaching puberty. (آتَيْناهُ حُكْماً وَعِلْماً): it has been said that its meaning is: We made him the one in control of judgement, so he judged within the king's dominion, and We gave him knowledge of judgement.

nahhas-irab:23-23.t:
(وَراوَدَتْهُ الَّتِي هُوَ فِي بَيْتِها عَنْ نَفْسِهِ): she was the king's wife. (وَغَلَّقَتِ الْأَبْوابَ): غلّق is for intensiveness/multiplicity, and one does not say غلق الباب; أغلق applies to both many and few, as al-Farazdaq said about Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, may Allah have mercy on him: [al-Basīṭ] 231-
ما زلت أفتح أبوابا وأغلقها ... حتّى أتيت أبا عمرو بن عمّار
(I kept opening doors and shutting them, until I came to Abū ʿAmr ibn ʿAmmār)
(وَقالَتْ هَيْتَ لَكَ): there are seven readings of it. Among the most weighty of what has been said about it, and the soundest in chain of transmission (isnād), is what al-Aʿmash related from Abū Wāʾil, who said: I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, may Allah have mercy on him, reading (وَقالَتْ هَيْتَ لَكَ). He said: I said: some people read it (هَيْتَ لَكَ). He said: I only read as I was taught. Abū Jaʿfar said: some of them relate it from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd from the Prophet ﷺ, and that is not far-fetched, because his saying:
"I only read as I was taught" indicates that it is traced back to the Prophet (marfūʿ). This reading, with fatḥa on the hāʾ and the tāʾ [هَيْتَ], is the sound one from the reading of Ibn ʿAbbās, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid and ʿIkrima, and Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read it so. Ibn Abī Isḥāq the grammarian read (وَقالَتْ هَيْتَ لَكَ) with fatḥa on the hāʾ and kasra on the tāʾ [هَيْتِ]. Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān [al-Sulamī] and Ibn Kathīr read (وَقالَتْ هَيْتَ لَكَ) with fatḥa on the hāʾ and ḍamma on the tāʾ [هَيْتُ]. These are three readings in which the hāʾ has fatḥa. Abū Jaʿfar [the reader], Shayba and Nāfiʿ read (وَقالَتْ هَيْتَ لَكَ) with kasra on the hāʾ and fatḥa on the tāʾ [هِيتَ]. Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read (وَقالَتْ هَيْتَ لَكَ) with kasra on the hāʾ, followed by a quiescent yāʾ, and the tāʾ with ḍamma [هِيتُ]. It is related from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid and ʿIkrima: (وَقالَتْ هَيْتَ لَكَ) with kasra on the hāʾ, followed by a quiescent hamza, and the tāʾ with ḍamma [هِئْتُ]. And from Ibn ʿĀmir and the people of Syria: (وَقالَتْ هَيْتَ لَكَ) with kasra on the hāʾ, with the hamza, and fatḥa on the tāʾ [هِئْتَ]. «[Translator's note: the source prints the Qur'anic words identically in every case; the bracketed vocalizations are added from the verbal descriptions.]»
Abū Jaʿfar said: «هيت لك» has fatḥa on the tāʾ because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, since it is a sound-word (ṣawt) that must not be inflected, and the fatḥa is light; so this is like your saying كيف and أين. Whoever puts a kasra on the tāʾ does so only because kasra is the original [vowel for resolving two quiescents]. Whoever puts a ḍamma does so also because of the meeting of two quiescents, and likens it to their saying «جوت» in driving a camel, which is said with ḍamma, fatḥa and kasra; «وجاه» has its meaning except that it is only said with kasra, and likewise «عاج» in driving a she-camel. As for the reading of the people of Medina, there are two views on it: one is that the fatḥa is because of the meeting of two quiescents, as has been mentioned; the other is that it is from هاء يهيء, like جاء يجيء, so that the meaning of «هيت» is "your appearance (hayʾa) has become fair", the hamza being lightened, and «لك» belongs to another phrase, as you say: لك أعني ("it is you I mean"). As for «لك» in «هيت لك», it is a clarification (tabyīn), as one says «سقيا لك» ("may you be watered"). ʿIkrima said: «هيت» means "come here", that is, to what I have invited you to; and «هيت لك» without hamza, and with hamza from هاء يهيئ. (قالَ مَعاذَ اللَّهِ) is a maṣdar (verbal noun); one says: عاذ معاذا ومعاذة وعياذا. (إِنَّهُ رَبِّي) is in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) for the hāʾ, and it may be nominative as the khabar (predicate). (إِنَّهُ لا يُفْلِحُ الظَّالِمُونَ): the hāʾ refers to the matter at hand (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and the clause is the khabar. «[Translator's note: the source prints «الأعمش بن أبي وائل»; rendered as "from Abū Wāʾil", which the isnād requires.]»

nahhas-irab:24-24.t:
(وَلَقَدْ هَمَّتْ بِهِ): a lām of emphasis; al-Khalīl claimed that «قد» is for expectation (tawaqquʿ). (وَهَمَّ بِها): we have already mentioned its meaning, and that some people said it is a case of fronting and postponement (taqdīm wa-taʾkhīr) [i.e. "he would have desired her had he not seen…"]. In my view this opinion is impossible, and not permissible in the language nor in any of the speech of the Arabs: one does not say "So-and-so stood up, if Allah wills" nor "So-and-so stood up, were it not for so-and-so". It has been said: his desire for her was the [natural] appetite and what crosses the heart, as one says ما يهمّني ذلك, that is, "I do not desire it". (لَوْلا أَنْ رَأى بُرْهانَ رَبِّهِ): (أن) is in the position of the nominative, and the response (jawāb) of لولا is omitted because the listener knows it. (كَذلِكَ): the kāf is in the position of the nominative, that is, "the matter of the proofs was thus"; and it may be in the position of the accusative, that is, "We showed him the proofs thus". (لِنَصْرِفَ عَنْهُ): the lām of purpose (lām kay), and what puts the verb in the accusative is [an implied] «أن».
(إِنَّهُ مِنْ عِبادِنَا الْمُخْلَصِينَ), that is, those made pure for conveying the Message, and those made pure for obedience to Allah, Majestic and Mighty.

nahhas-irab:25-25.t: (وَاسْتَبَقَا الْبابَ): the alif of «استبقا» is dropped in pronunciation because it is quiescent and the lām after it is quiescent, just as one says جاءني عبدا الله in the dual. Some Arabs say جاءني عبدا الله keeping the alif without hamza, combining two quiescents because the second is assimilated and the first is a letter of prolongation and softness; and some say جاءني عبدا الله keeping the alif and the hamza, as you say it in pause. «[Translator's note: the source prints «عبد الله» in all three examples; the dual عبدا الله is clearly intended.]» (وَقَدَّتْ قَمِيصَهُ): Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: القدّ is cutting, that is, she pulled and it tore. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is an instance of the inimitable concision of the Qurʾān, which gathers meanings together. The meaning is: Yūsuf ﷺ raced to the door, refusing her, in order to go out, and she raced him to the door to stand at it and prevent him from going out; and when he got ahead of her she pulled him so that he would not go out, and tore his shirt. (قالَتْ ما جَزاءُ مَنْ أَرادَ بِأَهْلِكَ سُوءاً): (ما) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is (أَنْ يُسْجَنَ). (أَوْ عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ) is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it. Al-Kisāʾī said: أو عذابا أليما is also permissible, in the sense of "or he be punished with a painful punishment".

nahhas-irab:26-27.t:
(وَشَهِدَ شاهِدٌ مِنْ أَهْلِها): we have mentioned a disagreement about it. What best fits the meaning — and Allah knows best — is that he was an intelligent, wise man whom the king consulted, and he brought this evidence. Had he been an infant, his testimony for Yūsuf ﷺ would have made it unnecessary to bring a proof from ordinary experience, because an infant's speaking is a miraculous sign, and would have been clearer than reasoning from ordinary experience. This does not contradict the ḥadīth "Four spoke while they were small", among them Yūsuf's witness; it would mean "young", not an old man. There is another clear proof in this: Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah have mercy on him, is the one who related the ḥadīth from the Prophet ﷺ, and the narration from him is widely transmitted (mutawātir) that Yūsuf's witness was not a child.
(إِنْ كانَ قَمِيصُهُ) is in the position of the jussive by the condition, and there is something problematic about it grammatically: it is said that conditional particles turn the past into the future, yet this is not so with كان. Al-Māzinī said: a verb of saying is implied. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said: this is because of the strength of كان, for it can express all verbs. Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said:
the meaning is: "if it be", that is, "if it be known"; for the knowing had not yet happened, and likewise the being, because it conveys [the sense of] knowing. (قُدَّ مِنْ قُبُلٍ): the khabar of كان is given as a past verb, as Zuhayr said: [al-Ṭawīl] 232-
وكان طوى كشحا على مستكنّة ... فلا هو أبداها ولم يتقدّم
(He had folded his flank over a hidden intent; he neither revealed it nor went ahead [with it])
Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read (إِنْ كانَ قَمِيصُهُ قُدَّ مِنْ قُبُلٍ فَصَدَقَتْ) with ḍamma on the qāf, the bāʾ and the lām [مِنْ قُبُلُ], and likewise «دبر». Abū Isḥāq said: he makes it a terminal adverb (ghāya), that is, "from its front" and "from its back". He said: «من قبلَ» and «من دبرَ» with fatḥa on the lām and the rāʾ are also permissible, likening it to a diptote, because it is definite and displaced from its normal pattern. «[Translator's note: "the lām" is as printed; the final letter of قبل is the lām, while the bāʾ is its middle letter.]»

nahhas-irab:29-29.t: (يُوسُفُ) is a singular vocative (munādā mufrad), that is, "O Yūsuf".

nahhas-irab:30-30.t:
(وَقالَ نِسْوَةٌ): one also says نُسوة; the plural of large number is نساء. «قد شغِفها» with kasra on the ghayn has been related, but in the speech of the Arabs only «شغَفها» with fatḥa on the ghayn is known; likewise (قَدْ شَغَفَها), that is, "it left her infatuated". (إِنَّا لَنَراها فِي ضَلالٍ مُبِينٍ),
that is, in this deed. This is the lām of emphasis, and here it does not occur with the past [verb], except that al-Akhfash permitted إنّ زيدا لنعم الرجل ("Zayd is indeed an excellent man"), because نعم is not conjugated. «[Translator's note: the source prints «ويقال: نسوة» without vocalization; the variant intended is presumably نُسوة.]»

nahhas-irab:31-31.t:
(فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ بِمَكْرِهِنَّ), that is, their faulting her and their scheming to disparage her. (أَرْسَلَتْ إِلَيْهِنَّ): there is an ellipsis in the wording, that is: she sent to them inviting them to a banquet, in order to bring them into what she had fallen into. (وَأَعْتَدَتْ) is from العتاد, which is anything you have made ready for something. (مُتَّكَأً): the soundest of what has been said about it is what ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "a sitting-place". As for the saying of the body of the exegetes that it is food, that is permissible on the implied form "food [for] a reclining-place", like «واسئل القرية»; and what indicates this ellipsis is (وَآتَتْ كُلَّ واحِدَةٍ مِنْهُنَّ سِكِّيناً), because the women's being present with knives can only be for food cut with knives.
The original of متّكأ is موتكأ; like it are متّزن and متّعد, from وزنت, وعدت and وكأت. One says: تكئ يتكأ تكأة. (وَآتَتْ كُلَّ واحِدَةٍ مِنْهُنَّ سِكِّيناً): two objects. Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ related that سكّين is masculine and feminine, and al-Farrāʾ recited: [al-Wāfir] 233-
فعيّث في السّنام غداة قرّ ... بسكّين موثّقة النّصاب
(He cut into the hump on a cold morning with a knife whose haft was firmly bound [fem.])
Al-Aṣmaʿī knows only the masculine for سكّين. (وَقالَتِ اخْرُجْ عَلَيْهِنَّ): with ḍamma on the tāʾ because of the meeting of two quiescents, since a kasra is heavy when followed by a ḍamma; and kasra on the tāʾ is according to the original. (وَقُلْنَ حاشَ لِلَّهِ), that is, "Allah forbid". Al-Aṣmaʿī related from Nāfiʿ that he read, as Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ read, وقلن حاشا لله, keeping the alif, which is the original; whoever drops it makes the lām after it a compensation for it. There are four dialectal forms of it: «حاشاك», «حاشا لك», «حاش لك» and «حشا لك»; and one says:
حشا زيدٍ and حاشا زيدا. Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: I heard Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] say: the accusative is preferable, because it has been established that it is a verb by their saying حاش لزيد, and nothing is dropped from a particle. Al-Nābigha said: [al-Basīṭ] 234-
وما أحاشي من الأقوام من أحد
(And I except no one among the tribes)
(ما هذا بَشَراً): (ما) was likened to ليس according to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh when the sentence is in its regular order. Sībawayh said:
"Many a particle is like this", that is, likened to another in some positions; then Sībawayh mentioned «تالله» and «لدن غدوة». The Kufans said: when the bāʾ was dropped, it took the accusative. The explanation of this, according to what Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā [Thaʿlab] said, is that when you say ما زيد بمنطلق, the position of the bāʾ[-phrase] is an accusative position, and likewise all the prepositions. He said: when the bāʾ was dropped, it took the accusative to indicate its position. He said: this is the view of al-Farrāʾ, and «ما» does not govern anything. The Basrans then held them to the consequence that they would have to say زيدٌ القمرَ, since the meaning is "like the moon". Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā answered this by saying: the bāʾ is more truly a preposition than the kāf, because the kāf can be a noun. Abū Jaʿfar said: only the Basrans' view is sound. This [Kufan] view is self-contradictory, because al-Farrāʾ explicitly permitted ما بمنطلق زيد, and recited: [al-Wāfir] 235-
أما والله أن لو كنت حرّا ... وما بالحرّ أنت ولا العتيق
(By Allah, if only you were free — but you are neither free nor of noble stock)
yet he explicitly forbade the accusative [there]. We know of no disagreement among the grammarians that ما فيك براغب زيد and ما إليك بقاصد عمرو are permissible, and that they then drop the bāʾ and use the nominative. The Basrans and the Kufans related ما زيد منطلق with the nominative, and the Basrans related that it is the dialect of Banū Tamīm, and recited: [al-Wāfir] 236-
أتيما تجعلون إليّ ندّا ... وما تيم لذي حسب نديد
(Do you make Taym a rival to me? Taym is no match for a man of noble lineage)
Al-Kisāʾī related that it is the dialect of Tihāma and Najd. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that the nominative is the stronger of the two options. Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: this is an error; the Book of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, and the language of His Messenger ﷺ are stronger and more fitting. (إِنْ هذا إِلَّا مَلَكٌ كَرِيمٌ): because of the superiority of the angels over humans.

nahhas-irab:33-33.t: (قالَ رَبِّ السِّجْنُ أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); the implied form is "entering the prison is dearer to me", that is, easier for me. Abū Ḥātim related that ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, may Allah be pleased with him, read السَّجن with a fatḥa on the sīn, and related that this is the reading of Ibn Abī Isḥāq, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Aʿraj and Yaʿqūb; it is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of سجنه سجنا ("he imprisoned him"). (وَإِلَّا تَصْرِفْ عَنِّي كَيْدَهُنَّ أَصْبُ إِلَيْهِنَّ): a condition and its requital (sharṭ wa-mujāzāt), that is: if You do not show me grace in avoiding sin, I will fall into it.

nahhas-irab:34-34.t: (فَاسْتَجابَ لَهُ رَبُّهُ), that is, He showed him grace in that. (فَصَرَفَ عَنْهُ كَيْدَهُنَّ): it has been said: because they were a group who had all tried to seduce him; and it has been said: it means the scheming of women [in general].

nahhas-irab:35-35.t:
(ثُمَّ بَدا لَهُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ ما رَأَوُا الْآياتِ لَيَسْجُنُنَّهُ): there are three views on it. The doctrine of Sībawayh is that «ليسجننّه» is in the position of the fāʿil (agent), that is, "it appeared to them [good] that they imprison him". Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said: this is an error; the fāʿil cannot be a clause; rather, the fāʿil is what بدا indicates, that is, "a [new] view (badāʾ) appeared to them", the fāʿil being omitted because the verb indicates it, as [the poet] said: [al-Wāfir] 237-
وحقّ لمن أبو موسى أبوه ... يوفّقه الّذي نصب الجبالا
(It is fitting that one whose father is Abū Mūsā be granted success by the One who set up the mountains)
The third view is that the meaning of «بدا له» in the language is: there appeared to him what he had not known; so the meaning is "then it appeared to them", that is, what they had not known, and this was omitted because there is an indication of it in the wording. The verb of saying is also omitted, that is: they said, "We will surely imprison him". This nūn is for emphasis; likewise the light [nūn], on which one pauses with an alif, as in (وَلَيَكُوناً) [Yūsuf: 32], in order to distinguish between them. Abū ʿUbayd said: one pauses on it with an alif because it resembles the tanwīn (nunation) in your saying رأيت رجلا. And the implied form is: "so they imprisoned him". «[Translator's note: the source prints «فحسبوه» ("so they reckoned him"), presumably a misprint for «فحبسوه» ("so they imprisoned him"); translated per the latter.]»

nahhas-irab:36-36.t: (وَدَخَلَ مَعَهُ السِّجْنَ فَتَيانِ) is the dual of فتى, which is of the roots with yāʾ; their saying الفتوّة [with wāw] is irregular (shādhdh). (قالَ أَحَدُهُما إِنِّي أَرانِي أَعْصِرُ خَمْراً): the implied form is "in sleep", which was then omitted. (نَبِّئْنا بِتَأْوِيلِهِ) is from the roots with hamza, which is why the yāʾ [i.e. the hamza seated on yāʾ] remains in it. Whoever lightens [the hamza] says نبّيْنا, and whoever substitutes for it says نبِّنا, dropping the yāʾ.

nahhas-irab:40-40.t: (ما تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ إِلَّا أَسْماءً سَمَّيْتُمُوها أَنْتُمْ وَآباؤُكُمْ): the second object is omitted because it is indicated, and the meaning is: "you named them gods of your own accord". (ما أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ) that in a Book. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: (مِنْ سُلْطانٍ), that is, any proof.

nahhas-irab:41-41.t:
(أَمَّا أَحَدُكُما فَيَسْقِي رَبَّهُ خَمْراً): some lexicographers related that سقاه and أسقاه are two dialectal forms with one meaning, as [the poet] said: [al-Wāfir] 238-
سقى قومي بني مجد وأسقى ... نميرا والقبائل من هلال
(May He water my people, Banū Majd, and water Numayr and the tribes of Hilāl)
Al-Aṣmaʿī said: I suspect this verse among the poetry of Labīd and imagine it is fabricated, because it brings two dialectal forms in one verse. Abū Jaʿfar said: what most lexicographers hold is that سقاه means "he handed it to him and he drank" or "he poured water down his throat", while أسقاه means "he provided him with water to drink". He, Majestic and Mighty, said: (وَأَسْقَيْناكُمْ ماءً فُراتاً) [al-Mursalāt: 27].

nahhas-irab:42-42.t: (وَقالَ لِلَّذِي ظَنَّ أَنَّهُ ناجٍ مِنْهُمَا): al-Kisāʾī said: the maṣdar (verbal noun) is نجوا and نجاء. (اذْكُرْنِي عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ), that is, mention what you have seen of me and the state I am in, of interpreting dreams and other things.

nahhas-irab:43-43.t:
(وَقالَ الْمَلِكُ إِنِّي أَرى سَبْعَ بَقَراتٍ سِمانٍ): the hāʾ [tāʾ marbūṭa of the numeral] is dropped to distinguish between masculine and feminine. Outside the Qurʾān, سبع بقرات سمانا is permissible as a naʿt (adjective) of (سبع), and likewise خضرا. Al-Farrāʾ said:
and like it is (سَبْعَ سَماواتٍ طِباقاً) [Nūḥ: 15].

nahhas-irab:44-44.t: (قالُوا أَضْغاثُ أَحْلامٍ), that is, "they are confused medleys". Al-Farrāʾ said: أضغاثَ أحلام is also permissible, that is, "you saw confused medleys of dreams". Abū Jaʿfar said: the accusative is far-fetched, because the meaning is: "you did not see anything that has an interpretation; these are only confused medleys of dreams". (وَما نَحْنُ بِتَأْوِيلِ الْأَحْلامِ بِعالِمِينَ): Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: the meaning is "in the interpretation of mixed-up dreams". «[Translator's note: the source prints «لم ترى», with the long alif retained after لم.]»

nahhas-irab:45-45.t: Abū Jaʿfar said: the original of (وَادَّكَرَ) is اذتكر. The dhāl is close in point of articulation to the tāʾ, but it was not permissible to assimilate it into it, because the dhāl is voiced (majhūr) and the tāʾ is voiceless (mahmūs); had they assimilated, the voicing would have been lost. So in place of the tāʾ they substituted a voiced letter, the dāl, which was more fitting than the ṭāʾ because the ṭāʾ is velarized (muṭbaq); it became اذدكر, and then they assimilated the dhāl into the dāl, and it became ادّكر. Al-Khalīl and Sībawayh related that some Arabs say اذّكر, assimilating the dāl into the dhāl because of the softness and laxity of the dhāl. One says: أمه يأمه إمها, "he forgot"; on this basis [one reads]: وادّكر بعد أمه ("and he remembered after forgetting"). «[Translator's note: the source prints «فصار إذ دكّر»; rendered as the intermediate form اذدكر.]»

nahhas-irab:46-46.t: (يُوسُفُ) is a singular vocative (munādā mufrad), and likewise (أَيُّهَا الصِّدِّيقُ): the one of abundant truthfulness.

nahhas-irab:47-47.t: (دَأَباً) is a maṣdar (verbal noun), because the meaning of (تزرعون) is "you toil persistently". Abū Ḥātim related from Yaʿqūb (دَأَباً) with a vowel on the hamza [دَأَبًا], and Ḥafṣ related it from ʿĀṣim. There are two views on it: the view of Abū Ḥātim is that it is from دئب. Abū Jaʿfar said: the lexicographers know only دأب. The other view is that it was given a vowel because it contains one of the guttural letters. «[Translator's note: the source prints the Qur'anic word identically for both readings; the variant described is دَأَبًا as against دَأْبًا.]»

nahhas-irab:48-48.t: (ثُمَّ يَأْتِي مِنْ بَعْدِ ذلِكَ سَبْعٌ شِدادٌ يَأْكُلْنَ): figuratively (majāzan), that is, their people eat. (ما قَدَّمْتُمْ لَهُنَّ), that is, what you have stored up for their sake. (إِلَّا قَلِيلًا) is accusative as an exception (istithnāʾ). (مِمَّا تُحْصِنُونَ), that is, of what you hold back in order to sow it.

nahhas-irab:50-51.t: (وَقالَ الْمَلِكُ ائْتُونِي بِهِ), that is: the messenger went and told him, and he said, "Bring him to me". (فَلَمَّا جاءَهُ الرَّسُولُ), that is, and ordered him to come out. (قالَ ارْجِعْ إِلى رَبِّكَ فَسْئَلْهُ ما بالُ النِّسْوَةِ), that is, so that he may learn the state of the women (اللَّاتِي قَطَّعْنَ أَيْدِيَهُنَّ), that is, so that he may know that I was imprisoned without any crime. (إِنَّ رَبِّي بِكَيْدِهِنَّ عَلِيمٌ): by this he indicated that they had schemed against him as the wife of al-ʿAzīz had schemed against him. The meaning is: the messenger went and told him, and he summoned them and said: (ما خَطْبُكُنَّ إِذْ راوَدْتُنَّ يُوسُفَ عَنْ نَفْسِهِ): the nūn is doubled because it corresponds to the mīm and the wāw in the masculine [plural].

nahhas-irab:52-52.t: (ذلِكَ) is in the position of the nominative, that is, "the matter is that". (لِيَعْلَمَ أَنِّي لَمْ أَخُنْهُ بِالْغَيْبِ), that is, I did not speak ill of him while he was absent; and so is betrayal. It has been said: this is from the words of Yūsuf ﷺ.

nahhas-irab:53-53.t: (وَما أُبَرِّئُ نَفْسِي) is [in the form] for intensiveness (taktīr), and likewise (إِنَّ النَّفْسَ لَأَمَّارَةٌ بِالسُّوءِ), that is, desiring it. (إِلَّا ما رَحِمَ رَبِّي) is in the position of the accusative as an exception (istithnāʾ).

nahhas-irab:54-54.t: (أَسْتَخْلِصْهُ لِنَفْسِي) is jussive (majzūm) because it is the response to the imperative. The meaning is: so they went and brought him, and [the wording] indicates this. (فَلَمَّا كَلَّمَهُ قالَ إِنَّكَ الْيَوْمَ لَدَيْنا مَكِينٌ), that is, established in [the position] we wish, with authoritative word. (أَمِينٌ): you need not fear treachery. «[Translator's note: the source prints «متمكّن من نريد» and «لا تخاف عذرا» ("an excuse"); rendered as if «مما نريد» and «غدرا» ("treachery"), which the context suggests.]»

nahhas-irab:55-55.t: (قالَ اجْعَلْنِي عَلى خَزائِنِ الْأَرْضِ إِنِّي حَفِيظٌ), that is, a guardian of them, (عَلِيمٌ), knowing where they deserve to be placed.

nahhas-irab:56-56.t: (يَتَبَوَّأُ مِنْها حَيْثُ يَشاءُ), that is, he settles. (نُصِيبُ بِرَحْمَتِنا مَنْ نَشاءُ), that is, by Our beneficence. (وَلا نُضِيعُ أَجْرَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ), that is, their reward; and by this He indicated that it was a reward for him.

nahhas-irab:58-58.t: (وَجاءَ إِخْوَةُ يُوسُفَ), that is: then the years of drought came, and Yūsuf's brothers came to Egypt to obtain provisions — this is an instance of the inimitable concision of the Qurʾān — (فَدَخَلُوا عَلَيْهِ فَعَرَفَهُمْ وَهُمْ لَهُ مُنْكِرُونَ), because they had left him as a boy, and did not imagine that after slavery he would reach that state.

nahhas-irab:59-59.t: (وَلَمَّا جَهَّزَهُمْ بِجَهازِهِمْ قالَ ائْتُونِي بِأَخٍ لَكُمْ مِنْ أَبِيكُمْ): he is Ibn Yāmīn [Benjamin], Yūsuf's brother from both his father and his mother. That is, he questioned them and talked with them until mention of his brother came up; this too is an instance of concision.

nahhas-irab:60-60.t: (فَإِنْ لَمْ تَأْتُونِي بِهِ فَلا كَيْلَ لَكُمْ عِنْدِي), that is, "I will not sell you anything". (وَلا تَقْرَبُونِ) is in the position of the jussive by the prohibition, which is why the nūn [of the indicative] has been dropped from it; and the yāʾ has been dropped because it is the end of a verse. Had it been a statement [rather than a prohibition], it would have been ولا تقربونَ with a fatḥa on the nūn. «[Translator's note: the source prints «فلا أبغيكم شيئا»; rendered as if «أبيعكم» ("I will sell you"), which the context suggests.]»

nahhas-irab:62-62.t: وقال لفتيته: this is the reading of the people of Medina, Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim. The rest of the Kufans read (وَقالَ لِفِتْيانِهِ), and this is the choice of Abū ʿUbayd, because he related from Hishām from Mughīra, who said: in the codex of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] it is «وقال لفتيانه». Abū Jaʿfar said: this contradicts the great mass [of the written text] (al-sawād al-aʿẓam), because in the written text there is no alif and no nūn in it; the agreed-upon written text is not to be abandoned for this broken chain of transmission (isnād munqaṭiʿ). Moreover, فتية is more fitting here than فتيان, because فتية among the Arabs is for a small number, and a small number is more fitting for placing the merchandise in the saddlebags. The original pattern of فتية is أفعلة, even though it has been formed as a diminutive on its [actual] wording.
